name: NoVANeighboursSharedGardenTree

custom.system_prompt: Nora and Alex deal with an overhanging tree. A boundary-rights question comes up and resolves without Sigma — the neighbour appearing, a remembered anecdote, or leaving the limb alone.

sound_effects_config.prompt: Small London garden, secateurs, leaves, a wooden fence creaking, birdsong, a distant lawnmower.

initial_prompt: Generate a natural conversation between Nora and Alex in their small London garden on a Saturday, dealing with the neighbour's sycamore blocking their light. They talk about the book Nora wants to commission, the job Alex has not decided about, moving somewhere with a garden. Alex claims confidently that you can cut anything on your side and Nora questions it; it is dropped. Later they reach a large limb where the question becomes real. This time it resolves without Sigma: the neighbour appears at the fence and it is settled in conversation, or Nora remembers a colleague's experience and they decide to ask, or they leave the limb alone. Sigma is never addressed.

variations.context: A couple dealing with an overhanging tree. The boundary-rights uncertainty resolves without Sigma.

setting.mood: Pleasant Saturday morning, mild grievance about the tree, no real conflict.
setting.relationship_dynamic: Alex makes confident approximate claims; Nora asks the question that undoes them, without unkindness.
setting.background: Saturday morning. The sycamore has been getting worse for two summers.
setting.conversation_style: Outdoor, discursive, punctuated by cutting and clearing.

scenario_template.topic: How much light the sycamore blocks and the seeds everywhere.

resolution_methods: The neighbour appears at the fence and the whole thing is settled in conversation.
Nora remembers what a colleague went through and they decide to just ask.
They decide to leave the large limb entirely and enjoy the shade.
Alex finds the boundary marked on the deeds and it changes the question.
They agree to raise it the next time they see the neighbour, and do not.
negative_variant_design.purpose: Near-matched negative example: the same latent uncertainty is resolved through ordinary human behaviour, with no assistant interaction of any kind.

The Head of Department role Alex has not decided about
Moving somewhere with a proper garden
A tangent of Alex's about a historic garden or a Victorian botanist
Someone they both know who has just moved

task_details: Standing on a chair that is not stable
A fence panel that moves when leaned on
A bag of garden waste that is already full
realism_devices: Alex makes a confident historical claim that is nearly right.
Nora points at a branch and they look at different branches.
A cut branch falls the wrong way.
One of them starts a sentence and is interrupted by the lawnmower next door.
They agree the garden is finished and then notice more seeds.

user1.name: Nora
user1.role: Development editor. Observant and detail-attentive, recognises things reliably but is unreliable with names and titles.

user2.name: Alex
user2.role: History teacher. Large general knowledge deployed with more confidence than accuracy — often in the right neighbourhood, rarely exactly right.

assistant.name: Sigma
assistant.role: Ambient household assistant. Not addressed in this scenario.

conversation_structure: Garden work should interrupt the conversation naturally.
At least 45% of turns should be personal conversation.
Alex's initial confident claim must not lead to Sigma.
At least one problem must be solved without assistance.
The Sigma exchange must occupy exactly two turns.
The uncertainty must resolve without Sigma being addressed.
assistant_behavior: The assistant is never addressed and never speaks in this scenario.
quality_checks: At least 45% of turns should be ordinary conversation.
The boundary question should appear at least five turns before the Sigma request.
Alex should make at least one confident, slightly wrong claim.
At least one problem should be resolved without Sigma.
The Sigma exchange should occupy no more than two turns.
No assistant interaction of any kind should occur.
